title: I Enforced the Trap-House Station Clock on the League Who Overstayed

parts.text: I stepped to station five at 10:04 a.m. and league captain Moss was already calling our numbered birds. The light said: ONE SQUAD. TWENTY-FIVE. STATION FOLLOWS THE CLOCK. I was forty-one, club scorer, holding a card that listed our round. Moss shrugged. "Leagues are the house." I photographed the light, the card, and his hulls on our pad. Then I asked for the station log. At 10:12 the range pinged why Moss's name was on our twenty-five. I kept my voice range-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A light is only a light until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The range can see Moss's hulls on our pad during our round.

social.video_title: He called our numbered birds past the station clock — Part 1/2
social.description: Trap house, a league on our pad, a twenty-five clock he posted. I logged the hulls. Would you have asked for the station log?

parts.text: Moss called it a practice until the range asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the light, and the hulls still. The station went back to our squad. Moss ran his own twenty-five and told the next league atmosphere was always about lead. Lead is a word leagues use when a clock exists. House policy now has a second line: LEAGUES ARE NOT THE HOUSE. I keep our card on a labeled clip. Moss brown-bags his jokes. The range finally looks like a round, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Station log, numbered birds, and a second line on the light. Was practice ever our pad?
